verdict.tagline: Tiny survival on a grand scale, best shared with friends.
for_you_if: you want a rich co-op survival experience
you enjoy base building and tactical combat
not_for_you_if: you will not create an Xbox account
you want flexible combat styles beyond parrying
you plan to play primarily solo

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering bugs that affect multiplayer synchronization, such as phantom water droplets and language settings causing crashes on the client player's end.

citations.review_text:
What a great game.

= Pros =

The combat is simple but very fun with lots of different combat styles to choose from. The gameworld is gorgeous and actually had me going, "Wow." when I first played. There's many unique areas to discover that the devs clearly put a ton of care and passion into designing and which were a joy to explore.

The survival mechanics are very well tuned to be important without being frustrating or annoying. Playing through the game co-op was an absolute blast. The writing is nothing special, which might be surprising if you know Obsidian from Fallout: New Vegas, but none of the writers from that game actually worked on this one, but it serves its purpose. The game has many hours of content that kept us engaged the whole time (much longer than the 8.1 hours it says as I write this-- steam just didn't properly track all of it).

= Cons =

Perhaps the biggest and only real downside were the frequent bugs affecting multiplayer synchronization. Floating, phantom water droplets you couldn't interact with were a basically constant occurence for whomever was the client player. Crashes and random disconnects were unfortunately not entirely unusual for both myself (on Windows 10) and my co-op partner (on Linux Mint), but mercifully the game's autosaves resulted in no loss of progress. Strangely, when I had my game's language to German, German text began 'leaking' into the client player's English game and soon caused his game to crash, forcing me to play in English as well.

= Other =

There's a number of things I would have liked to see in the game that weren't present, such as earthworms, centipedes, grasshoppers, rain-- suited to scale with temporary flooding and mud, climbing mechanics, and the conspicuously absent frog (since there are tadpoles). Perhaps we will see some of those in the sequel.

Overall fantastic, 9/10. Pick this game up instead of whatever "friendslop du jour" is out there.

After running this game at 1280x720p on low settings, and everything turned off that i could turn off, I get 30fps sometimes, with lows of 5-15fps. This game does not perform well at all. Some games can get away with 5 fps, as painful as that is, but this game requires perfect blocks, parrying, to not take damage from monsters. Fast paced, precision games need a high frame rate, at lest 60fps, or no lower than 30fps consistently, to allow players to time their inputs. Games can be punishing if they are fair, but seeing monsters glitch around at 5fps lows makes the game unplayable if you are going to play on medium or the hardest difficulty, woe.

I think eventually, everyone should try a good survival game on hard mode, but this game needs a lot of optimization before we can consider this a skill based game. I think single player might be fine, but multiplayer is broken. LAN play isn't an option in this game, so that leaves only online multiplayer, and I think the low frame rate comes from the constant resyncing of clients, even if they are on the same LAN. I'm glad games provide the option to play coop online, but this does not replace a more reliable LAN option.

Until this game gets optimized, I cannot recommend it unless you are going to play exclusively single player.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players deep into the game enjoy base defense and co-op save features despite repetitive audio and janky movement.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that character voice lines can become tiring by the end of the game.

citations.review_text: One of my favorite games ever. A survival game done right with fantastic progression and story bits to keep you going. A perfect setting for a survival game and they absolutely nailed the atmosphere and environment. The environmental storytelling is fantastic and the characters are great though some of their voice lines get tiring by the end. An extensive new game plus system with some new mechanics and items. One of the best features is a shared save system which makes it easy to play co op with friends, especially if you sometimes play at different times. Have had zero problems playing it cross platform. If you like survival games at all, then it's a must try.

This game is really fun, unique, and memorable! My favorite part of the game is the characters, I usually pick Willow because of the funny interactions she has with the other characters! The game also has a little something for everyone, whether you're more into combat, base building, exploration, or story! I'm entomophobic and arachnophobic, so I really appreciate the arachnophobia setting! Though I never really play this game by myself, I enjoy it much more when I'm playing with a friend. Even though I have entomophobia (the intense fear of insects), I love playing this game with my friends! I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun and unique survival game!

claims.claim: Base building includes creature attacks that require defensive placement and structures to protect against enemies.

citations.review_text:
One of the best survival crafting games I've played. The world is incredibly creative, and even after 80 hours I'm still finding new things to build, explore, and optimize. The progression from struggling against ants to taking on bosses and building huge bases feels really rewarding.

Base building is excellent, combat has a satisfying learning curve, and the backyard is packed with detail. Playing with friends makes it even better, but it's still a great solo experience.

My only real criticism is that I wish some of the automation was a bit more optimized. Late-game resource production can become fairly repetitive, and having a few more ways to streamline it would make long-term building even more enjoyable.

Overall, if you enjoy games like Valheim, Subnautica, or Raft, Grounded is an easy recommendation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the movement and parkour mechanics over thin branches can feel awkward and janky.

citations.review_text:
Can definitly recommend this game in Co-op. Haven´t played solo.
We were a group of three players, played till NG+5 and went for 100%.
This game really changed my view about nature. Seeing a hedge irl always remembers me now about the funny. yet a bit annoying parkour between branches xD

Lots of content for the price you pay, plus its replayable and has NG+. Lots to explore and discover so its worth the price. 
The big issue with this game is that it boasts an absolute garbage movement system which it forces you to use at every point and turn for collectibles and progress. Hosting multiplayer lobbies is also a pain since the game isn't that well optimized and also doesn't despawn your items. You constantly stutter-step and glitches are somewhat frequent.

Long game with great replayability and fun progress system that isn't straight forward. The parkour mechanics were iffy and the game in itself was pretty bad optimized, since nothing in the world despawned. Otherwise a fun experience with decent achievements :)

Yet a mutation and a few items give bonuses and remove the ability to perfect block making you think a different playstyle is possible but it's really not.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the combat system relies heavily on a perfect parry or block mechanic, making boss fights difficult for players who struggle with timing.

citations.review_text: Dear god the combat suck's, you DO NOT get more powerful not by much. The more you play everything just feels more and more of a pain combat wise, just such a time sink and it's so difficult, I enjoy doing the parrying but sheesh  dude really. The the Brood Mother fight, the base one, so many much stuff's, I can't at all see how I can make this combat fun. Then there's new game plus which I'd be super happy to play through up to +2 or +3 but everthing just have super duper lot's of health. The combat isn't bad but ffs it's a game of worthless ranged damage and genuinely exhausting. Besides long term play this game is super super super fun by a whole lot, running around is lovely, specially with a lot of speed boost. Being able to make ziplines where ever is very lovely and nice too! Never made enough but enjoyed this game tons! Just wish combat wasn't proper training to become a god!

I had Grounded in my queue to play for the longest time, good reviews but the whole 'honey I shrunk the kids thing' didn't really appeal (it still doesn't), and I had played Smalland already which seemed very similar... but I can 100% confirm its a game any survival fan needs to play.

There are very few fully formed Survival games on the market, many are stuck in early access.. but this one has clearly had many iterations of improvement, and its 95% a fully fleshed out top title game.. all the menus and the crafting and the quality of life, variety of weapons, the world.. its all quality.

[b]Game Difficulty:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Perfect Parry/Block:[/b] One criticism (for my skill level) is that the game leans heavily into that perfect parry/block mechanic that so many games do now.. and if you are really good at that.. the game is almost trivialised, bosses become 'easy', but if you cant.. the game becomes really very difficult.. and I fall into that latter camp.. however.. if you don't mind giving up some achievements.. you can adjust the game difficulty in many ways which saves the game for sure.. I changed so many things, including monster health down to a 0.25x multiplier (so they hit for 100% damage but have 25% health).. stamina use off.. keep backpack on death (can die to teleport home), no fall deaths, etc etc.. and I still found the game super challenging.. so the fact I could change settings opened the game to me where I probably would have given up otherwise.. death runs for bags are never fun if you are dieing regularly, and the bosses are tough too.. 

[*]  [b]New Game+:[/b] The other great thing is you can genuinely play this game 'until you have had enough', I am currently on New Game+ Level 5 (NG+5), that means its my 6th run through the game, every run becomes increasingly harder, but there is new loot and upgrades that makes it rewarding to do it again.. I love that.. also.. you keep all your builds/base/everything, so you keep most of your work in…
